chunks: He said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed me from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them, who said:

Among the words Allah confided to Musa ibn Imran, peace be upon him, was: 'O Musa! I have not created any creation more beloved to Me than My believing servant. And when I test him, it is only for what is good for him. And I know best what is good for My servant. So let him be patient with My trials, let him be grateful for My bounties, and let him be pleased with My decree. I shall write him among the truthful ones with Me, when he acts according to what pleases Me and obeys My command.'

key_terms.أبتليه: I test him - divine trials as purification
key_terms.الصديقين: the truthful ones - the highest spiritual rank after prophets
key_terms.ناجى: confided / whispered - divine intimate conversation (munajat) with Musa

ai.seo_question: What did Allah reveal to Prophet Musa about why He tests His believing servants?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq relays a divine revelation given to Prophet Musa, in which Allah explains His special love for the believing servant and the wisdom behind trials. The divine speech establishes that suffering is purposeful, and the conditions for being inscribed among the truthful (siddiqin) are patience in tribulation, gratitude for blessings, and contentment with divine decree -- the three pillars of spiritual excellence in Islamic theology.
word_analysis: and let him be grateful for

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 2. He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan reported to me from his father, who reported from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Dawood ibn Farqad, who reported that: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, said:

Among the words spoken to Allah to Musa son of Imran, peace be upon him, He revealed: "O, Musa! I have not created anything more beloved and preferred to Me than My faithful, believing servants. And when I try him, it is for his own good. I take away from him what he desires most, for his own good; and I grant him for his own benefit. And I know best what is beneficial for My servant. So, it is for him to be patient, when I try him, to be grateful when I bless him with My bounties, and he should remain pleased with My judgement. (Then) I write his name among My Truthfuls when he acts according to My pleasure and obeys My orders."
